results.name: lossless save of a file with no extLst: every added x14 rule lands in a new worksheet extLst, validates against the MS-XLSX schema, and nothing x14-only is written as a 2007 rule
reopen: the reader gets back every added rule with its x14 properties, and the reopened workbook draws exactly what the edited one drew
a file that already has an x14 ext (Excel-written corpus file): the ext and its <x14:conditionalFormattings> are reused, Excel's own x14 rules stay byte-identical, priorities stay unique
changing an imported x14 data bar rewrites it under the SAME id (no orphan x14 rule, no dangling link); a duplicated rule gets a fresh id
a worksheet whose SpreadsheetML namespace is prefixed (x:worksheet) gets a prefixed x:extLst / x:ext; the x14 elements keep their own namespace
second-order: an existing CF ext whose x14 namespace uses another prefix (a:conditionalFormattings) is extended in place — never a second container in the same ext
re-saving the patched file unchanged is a no-op for conditional formatting (no duplicated x14 rules), and removing an added x14-only rule removes exactly it
new-file export (writeXlsxWorkbook): cross-sheet thresholds go x14-only too, and the reader reads an x14-only data bar back
oracle negative controls: the checker rejects each defect it claims to catch (wrong x14 child order, missing xm:sqref, duplicate id, dangling link, cross-sheet 2007 formula, extLst not last)
